findings.summary: In the migrate-loop's non-201/409 case branch, the rewrite drops `failed=$((failed + 1))` that existed in the pre-refactor code. The status is still correctly captured and branched on (matching the brief's 'callers can reliably branch on status codes' requirement), but the failure branch no longer records the failure: `failed` stays 0 for any migrate call that errors (5xx, malformed payload, auth issue, etc.), so the end-of-run summary undercounts failures and the final gate `[[ "$failed" -eq 0 ]] || exit 1` will exit 0 even though repos failed to mirror. For a nightly unattended backup cron job, this silently defeats monitoring/alerting on failures — exactly the kind of bug the resilience rework was supposed to make visible, not hide.
